coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For The Shame
You Carry In Silence
coverDek: Five prayers for the story you've never said out loud — the shame that isn't guilt, because you already apologized for the guilt. Five different voices, one steady God who was never disappointed in you.

points.hook: Lord, there's a version of my story I have never told anyone out loud.
paragraphs: I've edited it so many times for so many rooms that I'm not even sure I remember the true shape of it anymore — only that somewhere under all the editing is the part I'm convinced would change how people look at me. But You were there for the unedited version. You watched it happen in real time, with nothing smoothed over, and You never once turned Your face away. Let me stop managing the story in front of You. Let me just tell it to You plainly tonight, and let me believe what Your word says is true on the other side of telling it.
points.verseText: They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed.

points.hook: I decree it today: there is no condemnation left for me to carry!
paragraphs: I break every chain of shame that has outlived its reason for existing, in the name of Jesus! The thing is forgiven, the blood has already spoken, and I refuse to keep paying a debt the cross already closed! Shame, you do not get to sit at my table one more day — I walk after the Spirit now, not after the flesh, and the verdict over my life was settled at Calvary, not in my memory! I am free, and I say so out loud!
points.verseText: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

points.hook: Notice how your shoulders curl in when you remember it.
paragraphs: Shame doesn't just live in your thoughts — it lives in the way you shrink in a doorway, the way your eyes drop before anyone's even looked at you, the flinch that shows up in your body before your mind finishes the memory. God's promise to a confounded, confused people wasn't just emotional — it covered the whole body: not ashamed, not confounded, not put to shame. Let your shoulders come down as you pray this. Let your chin lift. That's not performance — that's the shame actually leaving.
points.verseText: Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed: neither be thou confounded; for thou shalt not be put to shame.

points.hook: Somebody reading this has never told their own church the real version.
paragraphs: Family, we've gotten so good at the testimony with the rough edges sanded off that some of us have never let anyone see the actual before. But a family that only meets your edited self was never going to be able to carry the real weight with you anyway. Come boldly — not carefully, not strategically, boldly — to the throne where mercy is already waiting, and let the people God has put around you practice being the body of Christ for the parts of your story you've been carrying alone.
points.verseText: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

points.hook: Child, I was not holding My breath waiting to be disappointed in you.
paragraphs: You keep bracing for the moment I finally see the whole thing and pull back — but I already saw the whole thing, long before you were brave enough to look at it yourself, and I didn't pull back then either. I am not managing my distance from you. I am in the middle of you, mighty to save, and over the very thing you're most ashamed of, I am not holding a grudge — I am singing. Rest in that tonight. You are not a disappointment I am tolerating. You are a child I am singing over.
points.verseText: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named what you've been hiding, don't just scroll past it — pray it out loud tonight. Come back tomorrow for the next series.
